Bridal mehndi is practiced across South Asia, the Middle East, and North Africa with distinct regional traditions. In many cultures, bridal henna is applied by a senior married woman believed to bring good fortune.

faq.q: When should a bride get mehndi applied before the wedding?
faq.a: Apply mehndi 1-2 days before the wedding. The stain develops over 24-48 hours, reaching peak color by the wedding day.

faq.q: How long does bridal mehndi take?
faq.a: Full bridal mehndi (both hands and feet) typically takes 4-8 hours depending on design complexity.

faq.q: How can I make my bridal mehndi darker?
faq.a: Leave paste on overnight, apply lemon-sugar sealant, keep hands warm, and avoid water for 12-24 hours after removal.

title: Charming African Lotus Pattern Mehndi Design for Back Hand
descriptionParagraphs: A stunning african mehndi design tailored for the back of the hand, featuring bracelet cuff and ring pattern. Rated as Expert, this pattern is perfect for a party.

Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than the palm, so the stain is usually lighter and fades sooner. Leaving the paste on for longer helps the colour develop. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.

Application tips: Scrape the dried paste off instead of washing it, and keep the area away from water for the first 12 to 24 hours. The stain starts orange and darkens to reddish brown over 24 to 48 hours as it oxidises.

image.alt: African Lotus Pattern mehndi design for back hand — charming henna pattern

faq.q: How long should I leave the mehndi paste on?
faq.a: Keep the paste on for at least four to six hours. Many people leave it overnight for a darker stain.

faq.q: Why does my mehndi look orange at first?
faq.a: Fresh henna stains are orange. The colour deepens to reddish brown over the next 24 to 48 hours as the dye oxidises.

faq.q: Is black henna safe?
faq.a: Natural henna is never black. Products sold as black henna often contain PPD, a hair-dye chemical that can cause skin reactions, so they are best avoided.

faq.q: Is Arabic mehndi good for beginners?
faq.a: Yes, Arabic mehndi is considered the best starting style for beginners. The flowing, larger patterns are more forgiving than intricate Indian designs.

faq.q: How dark does Arabic mehndi stain?
faq.a: On palms and fingertips, Arabic mehndi stains a deep reddish-brown. On the back of the hand, expect a lighter orange-brown.
